items.name: Blueberries or strawberries
items.why: The sweet thing that isn’t candy — whichever is in season.

items.name: Avocado
items.why: A whole-food fat that needs no cooking.

items.name: Baby spinach
items.why: Goes into eggs, soup, or a salad with no prep at all.

items.name: Carrots and bell peppers
items.why: Both keep for weeks and get eaten raw when you’re hungry.

items.name: Sweet potatoes
items.why: More nutrient-dense than a white potato, and sweet enough to need nothing on it. Bake a tray, eat off it all week.

items.name: Whatever fruit is in season
items.why: Apples, citrus, stone fruit, melon, grapes, pears. In season is cheaper and tastes like something.

items.name: Bananas and apples
items.why: The two most kids will actually eat, and no packaging.

items.name: Chicken thighs, bone-in
items.why: More forgiving than breasts and cheaper per pound — hard to dry out.

items.name: Wild-caught salmon
items.why: Wild when the budget allows. A whole-food-standard call, not a verdict on farmed.

items.name: Pasture-raised eggs
items.why: Pasture-raised is the one egg label with real meaning behind it.

items.name: Plain whole-milk Greek yogurt
items.why: Plain, so you’re not buying dessert — add your own fruit.

items.name: Canned black beans
items.why: The cheapest real protein in the building — rinse them to cut the sodium.

items.name: Dried lentils
items.why: No soaking, done in twenty minutes, and they stretch a meal.

items.name: Extra-virgin olive oil — dark bottle
items.why: Look for a HARVEST date, not just “best by” — dark glass keeps it from going rancid.

items.name: Frozen broccoli or green beans
items.why: Picked ripe and frozen fast — cheaper than fresh and it never spoils.

berries_picking.headline: The carton’s underside decides, not the berries on top.
berries_picking.do: Flip the container and check for juice stains or fuzz.
berries_picking.tier_note: That berries decay from the bottom under their own weight, and do not ripen after picking, is settled postharvest handling — and it is why the underside is the check.

teaser.look_for_first: A dry, unstained bottom on the carton. That is the whole check.

produce_ripeness_by_item.topic: How to pick it, item by item
produce_ripeness_by_item.headline: Pick up two and take the heavier one.
produce_ripeness_by_item.do: Smell the stem end on anything that ripens after picking.
produce_ripeness_by_item.tier_note: Weight tracking water content is physical, and it is why the heavier of two is the better one.

teaser.look_for_first: Cantaloupe: creamy gold under the netting, a sweet smell at the stem end, slight give.

produce_seasonality.headline: Buy what is piled high and cheap this week.
produce_seasonality.do: Walk the farmers’-market table before the produce aisle.
produce_seasonality.tier_note: Reading the season off the pile is a shopping habit offered as a standard, not a nutrition claim.

teaser.look_for_first: The cheapest, most abundant produce this week is usually what’s in season.

air_chilled_chicken.headline: Air-chilled. A water-chilled bird absorbs the bath it was cooled in.
air_chilled_chicken.do: Check the package for “retained water up to”. That percentage is water.
air_chilled_chicken.tier_note: Retained water is a disclosed number. Preferring air-chilled is a standard about handling.

teaser.look_for_first: ‘Air-chilled’ is printed on the package when it applies.

salmon_wild_vs_farmed.headline: Wild. Farmed is a different fish, fed and penned.
salmon_wild_vs_farmed.do: Take the frozen sockeye from the freezer case, not the fresh Atlantic.
salmon_wild_vs_farmed.tier_note: The feed, the added pigment and the pens are documented facts. Holding out for wild on top of them is the standard.

teaser.look_for_first: Frozen wild Alaskan is often cheaper and fresher than ‘fresh’ farmed that has been in transit.

egg_labels.topic: Egg labels, and what the hen ate
egg_labels.headline: Soy-free and corn-free first, then organic, then pasture-raised.
egg_labels.do: Check the small regional cartons. That is where a feed claim appears.
egg_labels.tier_note: What each carton word is allowed to mean is defined. Ranking feed above room is the standard.

teaser.look_for_first: ‘Soy-free’ and ‘corn-free’ are the only words on the carton about the ration.

yogurt_plain_vs_flavored.headline: Plain, big tub. Add your own fruit.
yogurt_plain_vs_flavored.do: Take the big plain tub, not the single-serve fruit cups.
yogurt_plain_vs_flavored.tier_note: The added-sugar difference is printed on the panel. Buying plain and sweetening it is the standard.

teaser.look_for_first: Plain over flavored — sweeten it yourself with fruit.

beans_dried_vs_canned.headline: Dried. Same bean, a fraction of the price, and your own salt.
beans_dried_vs_canned.do: Fill a bag from the bulk bin. Whole beans, no split skins.
beans_dried_vs_canned.tier_note: That rinsing removes much of the canning sodium is measured, and beans as the cheapest real protein is arithmetic.

teaser.look_for_first: Dried beans cost a fraction of canned per serving.

olive_oil_grades.headline: Extra virgin, a recent harvest date, one country.
olive_oil_grades.do: Read “product of”, not “packed in” — they name different countries.
olive_oil_grades.tier_note: The grades are legal definitions with a taste panel behind them, and the origin wording is regulated. Both are readable off the bottle.

teaser.look_for_first: Extra virgin: mechanically extracted, no heat or solvent, taste-panel tested.

frozen_vs_fresh_produce.headline: Frozen. Cheaper, no waste, and in season all year.
frozen_vs_fresh_produce.do: Read the bag’s ingredient list for one word: the vegetable.
frozen_vs_fresh_produce.tier_note: Freezing at harvest and the losses across days in transit are both well documented.

teaser.look_for_first: Check the bag lists just the vegetable/fruit — no sauces or added sugar.
